verdict.rationale: a-Shell ships its own Apple Shortcuts actions (Execute Command, Put File, Get File) for building scripted file-processing automations, and these can run "in Extension" rather than in the app, though with the caveat that this "won't always work." There is no first-party scheduler or trigger-action rules surface: the relay evidence says "no trigger-action rules surface exists," and `.profile` runs only when a window opens. Recurring or autonomous triggering would have to come from the host platform, which earns no credit here. Missing for 10: a native scheduling/recurring trigger mechanism, documented reliable background execution, trigger-action rules, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: You can write complex Shortcuts to download, process and release files using a-Shell commands.
`Execute Command`, which takes a list of commands and executes them in order.
You can force a specific shortcut to run "in App" or "in Extension", with the warning that it won't always work.
